title: Positions 4 and 5
author: Dr. Can's Chess Clinic (Can Kabadayi)

source.title: How to Stop Hanging Your Pieces: 3 Common Blunders Explained

description: Two more positions: choose the right recapture on d4, then punish the opponent who chose wrong.
permissionNote: Lesson for a day of the Stop Hanging Pieces course; the course permission (pending) governs it.

chapterData.name: Rook or queen takes d4?

children.comment: Take back with the rook. The knight on e7 is still a loose piece, but it isn't hanging, so you don't lose anything. Stay careful: with a loose piece, watch for double attacks and remove-the-defender tricks.
Also good by the engine: it hits the knight on h4 first. Can takes back with the rook.
Your queen was the main guard of the loose knight on e7. Move her away and you turn a loose piece into a hanging one: Qxe7.

moves.comment: Look at the knight on e7. It's attacked once, by the queen on e2, and guarded once, by your queen on f6. Equal attackers and defenders is what Can calls a loose piece. A move ago it was protected, because the e3 pawn blocked the file; exd4 made it loose.

chapterData.intro: The third way to hang a piece. White is about to take on d4 with the pawn, and then you have to recapture: with the rook or with the queen? Avoid the blunder.

chapterData.name: Punishing ...Qxd4

children.comment: Take it. Black turned a loose knight into a hanging one by moving its defender.

moves.comment: Black's queen was the main guard of the knight on e7, and it just walked away. The loose piece is now hanging.

chapterData.intro: Now play White. Black has to recapture on d4. Can says moves like the next one are the norm in beginner games, because people don't track which pieces are loose.

chapterData.name: Punishing Nxe5

children.comment: The hanging knight on e5 is captured. A loose piece plus a king in the center gave Black the double attack.
Any answer to the check is the same story: the knight is now hanging and White has no time to rescue it.
Blocking with the knight changes nothing: the knight on e5 is still hanging.
The same here: White deals with the check, and the knight on e5 falls.
Qa5+ hits the king on e1 and the loose knight on e5 at once. White must answer the check, so there's no time to save the knight.

moves.comment: On e5 the knight becomes loose, with zero attackers and zero defenders. It can't be captured directly, but care is required. Find the double attack.

chapterData.intro: Should White grab the pawn on e5? Blunder-check Nxe5 with Can's terms. Right now the knight on f3 is very protected: attacked zero times and guarded twice. You have Black.
